title: Credential value present only in a Base64 or hex form
description: An authored base value (a credential-shaped literal) whose bytes appear in the input only after one Base64 or Base16 (hex) encoding, alone in a field or inside other text. Terms: standard Base64 uses '+' and '/', URL-safe Base64 uses '-' and '_' in their place (RFC 4648 sections 4 and 5); padded text ends in '=' to a multiple of four characters, unpadded text omits it; hex is lower, upper or mixed case; whole-value means the encoded text is the entire value of its field, embedded means it sits inside longer text; single layer means one encoding of the base value. For an ASCII base the two Base64 alphabets give identical text unless the base holds '>' or '~' (which encode to '+') or '?' (which encodes to '/') at a byte offset whose remainder modulo three is two, and padding appears only when the base length is not a multiple of three.
semantics: Four questions are kept apart and none is answered here: (1) observation, whether anything reports on the input; (2) decoded-family recognition, whether the decoded bytes are attributed to the family of the base; (3) source coverage, whether a reported range covers the encoded source span that stands for the base; (4) actual-output protection, whether what the product emits no longer carries the base. The fixture facts are only these: which authored base, which encodings in which order, the decoded digest and length, and the byte range of the encoded text. Whether a decoder runs, whether a decoded credential is acted on, and with what action are decisions of the owning product and are not stated by any fixture of this scenario. A decoder succeeding on a value never makes that value a secret: encoded hashes, public text and placeholders are the benign counterparts and project their own benign Case or Scenario.

applicability.rationale: The reasoning is the same for every family and for provider-less literals: only the base value differs, so it is stated once and instantiated by a plan over authored bases.

evidenceBasis.rationale: RFC 4648 defines the encodings (alphabets, padding, case), which settles what each representation is, but no source read settles whether an encoded credential must be treated as the credential, nor where protection must apply. Searched: RFC 4648; the family sources already cited by the families' contracts, which describe only the plaintext format. Not found: any provider statement about a credential held in Base64 or hex. The decision is a maintainer's (candidate: the decoded base is the credential and the encoded text is the range to cover). Carrier-mandated encodings with their own standards (HTTP Basic, Docker auth, Kubernetes data) are separate research and are not generalised from here.

sources.supports: Defines the standard Base64 alphabet, the URL and filename safe alphabet that replaces '+' and '/' with '-' and '_', when padding may be omitted, and Base16 as hexadecimal digits; implementations reject characters outside the alphabet.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from RFC 4648 read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. The 2026-10-03 stress run motivated the question and is not an input; its counts are not evidence.
